question: Your team uses Claude Code to generate a new payment validation module. A developer then asks the same Claude Code session to review the generated changes before merging. The review reports no problems, but a teammate later finds several logic errors in the module. Which change would most effectively improve the quality of this review?

options.text: Resume the generation session with --resume in the pipeline so the reviewer keeps full knowledge of the original design decisions.
options.reason: Resuming the generation session carries over the same context, and the guide says this shared context makes the review less effective than an independent instance.

options.text: Ask the same session to report its findings with --output-format json and --json-schema so the results are machine-parseable.
options.reason: These flags only make the output structured; the review still runs in the generating session, so it is still less effective than an independent review instance.

options.text: Run the review in a separate Claude Code instance that starts without the context of the session that generated the code.
options.reason: The guide states that an independent review instance reviews changes more effectively than the same session that generated them, because that session keeps its own generation context.

options.text: Add an instruction in the same session that tells Claude to review its own changes more critically before approving them.
options.reason: The review still runs in the session that generated the code, so the session context isolation problem that the guide describes remains.
